budget_items.what_was_said: The finance committee reviewed DESE-reported staffing data showing total school FTEs grew from FY16 through FY25, continuing to rise even after COVID relief funds dried up.
Enrollment peaked in FY19 and declined by FY25, even as total staffing continued to grow over the same period, described as roughly 80 fewer students and about 40 more staff.
Instructional staff levels were described as essentially flat from FY16 to FY25, with a peak in FY18.
Paraprofessional staffing grew from FY16 to FY25, prompting a question about what ratio of paraprofessionals to students should be expected.

budget_items.what_was_said: Instructional support staff and special-education shared instructional support staff both grew over the ten-year period reviewed.
Special education related staff were described as fairly flat across the period.
Office/clerical support and administrator FTEs both grew over the ten years reviewed, with administrators peaking at one point.
A member flagged a large percentage increase in a clerical staffing line and suggested it be asked about, while noting there may be a good explanation.
Revenue the schools receive from out-of-district students has fallen sharply over roughly the last six to seven years, tied to a school committee enrollment policy decision.

A member said the district changed its accounting practice for the circuit breaker/out-of-district placement line, which made costs on that line appear to have grown by roughly this amount between FY24 and now.
The athletics revolving account ran roughly this much in the negative, requiring funds to be moved from the regular school budget to cover it.
A member noted the town is approaching this amount in school lunch revenue, cited as an example of revenue not shown alongside expenses in current budget presentations.
A member noted the school committee had recently approved another line transfer of this amount for athletic transportation, citing it as evidence of financial management concerns.
A member noted last year's override was about this amount while the district simultaneously chose to let out-of-district revenue fall by roughly half that much.
A member suggested that rather than seeking an override every year, the town could ask for a larger override (30-40% more) covering multiple years to avoid annual override fatigue.

minutes.headline: Finance Committee backs a new joint 'tri-board' process with select board & school committee to build the FY27 budget
minutes.summary: The Finance Committee discussed and largely endorsed the town manager's proposal for a monthly 'tri-board' process (finance committee, select board, school committee together) to build the FY27 budget starting in July, aiming to surface issues like overrides, consolidations and financial forecasting earlier than in past years. The committee also reviewed historical school staffing, enrollment, out-of-district revenue and revolving-fund data raising questions about financial management, while a resident publicly opposed the tri-board concept.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee agreed in principle to a monthly 'tri-board' process with the Select Board and School Committee to build the FY27 budget, starting in July.
Members reviewed ten years of district staffing data showing enrollment declined while total school staffing kept rising, including growth in paraprofessional and clerical positions.
A member said the district changed its accounting practice for out-of-district placement costs, which affected how that budget line appears to have grown between FY24 and now.
A resident spoke against the tri-board process, arguing a large joint meeting would accomplish little and citing difficulty getting financial information from the school department.
The committee set its next meeting for July 10, with none scheduled for June 26.

why_it_matters: A joint tri-board process would change how the FY27 school and town budgets are shaped before residents see a warrant article, potentially surfacing overrides or consolidations earlier than in past years.
The staffing-versus-enrollment questions raised touch the school budget's biggest cost driver and will likely resurface as documentation requests in the tri-board sessions.
A change in how out-of-district placement costs are accounted for affects how budget-to-budget comparisons on that line should be read, not necessarily how much is actually being spent.
